_comment: R0 SEED worldwide ceremony-recognition registry per ADR-2605263400. Each entry maps, INFORMATIONALLY, whether and how a religious / covenant rite (marriage, naming, funeral) carries any civil-law recognition in a jurisdiction, and the SEPARATE civil-registration step a member must perform themselves. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class) and does NOT confer civil status. LONG-TAIL WORLDWIDE DEEPENING (2026-06-02): merged 27 additional jurisdictions across four buckets (EU-REST: Italy/Spain/Poland/Netherlands/Ireland/Norway/Sweden; asia-rest: PRC/Taiwan/Hong Kong/Thailand/Vietnam/Indonesia/Philippines/Malaysia; AMERICAS-REST: Argentina/Chile/Colombia/Peru/Canada-Québec; MEA-OCEANIA: New Zealand/South Africa/Israel/Kenya/Nigeria/UAE/Egypt) to broaden civil-recognition wayfinding beyond the original core. ALL entries ship verificationStatus=unverified-seed: per G14, NO live reliance may occur against an unverified entry — these MUST be human/Council-verified (and re-checked within the freshness window) before any guidance is surfaced. Per G8, every entry cites legalBasis + provenance and never fabricates 手続き / 様式 / 根拠法令; honest coverage over inflated counts. authority / channel / legalBasis below are best-effort public references as of 2026-06-02 and are EXPECTED to drift (esp. per-jurisdiction / per-municipality variation) — treat them as wayfinding scaffolds, not authoritative, never live use, and not legal advice (UPL boundary).

recognitions.title: Civil Marriage Notification (婚姻届 / kon'in-todoke)
recognitions.authority: Municipal office (市区町村役場) of the residence, domicile-of-record (本籍地), or place of either party — Ministry of Justice Civil Affairs Bureau (法務省民事局) supervising
recognitions.channel: Member's local 市区町村役場 戸籍課 (city/ward/town family-register desk); form template e.g. https://www.moj.go.jp/MINJI/minji02.html
recognitions.legalBasis: 民法第739条 (Civil Code Art. 739 — marriage takes legal effect ONLY upon notification under the Family Register Act; 届出婚主義 / formal-notification principle) read with 戸籍法 (Family Register Act, Act No. 224 of 1947), filing requires the parties' signatures and two adult witnesses
recognitions.notes: CORE BOUNDARY: a musubi covenant marriage ceremony (Reformed 万人祭司 — no clergy class, no officiant authority) carries ZERO civil-law effect in Japan. Japan recognizes NO 'religious marriage' as such; only the 婚姻届 創設的届出 (constitutive notification) creates a legally married couple. Members who wish civil-married status MUST file the 婚姻届 themselves at a municipal office — musubi neither files it nor acts as a recognized officiant. Drift: form layout and witness rules are stable but municipal counter hours/online-pre-fill options vary; confirm at the member's own 役場. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Birth Notification incl. Legal Naming (出生届 / shussei-todoke)
recognitions.authority: Municipal office (市区町村役場) 戸籍課 of the place of birth, parents' residence, or domicile-of-record — Ministry of Justice Civil Affairs Bureau supervising
recognitions.channel: Member's local 市区町村役場 戸籍課; overview e.g. https://www.moj.go.jp/MINJI/minji07.html
recognitions.legalBasis: 戸籍法第49条 (Family Register Act Art. 49 — birth must be notified within 14 days, child's given name entered) and 戸籍法第50条 + 戸籍法施行規則第60条 (Art. 50 + Enforcement Reg. Art. 60 — name must use permitted 常用漢字/人名用漢字/かな characters)
recognitions.notes: BOUNDARY: a musubi naming / dedication covenant ceremony (Reformed 万人祭司, no clergy) confers NO civil status and does NOT set the child's legal name. The child's legal name is fixed only by the 出生届 the parents file themselves, subject to the permitted-character restriction. A ceremonial/covenant name is a spiritual act with no registry effect. Drift: the 人名用漢字 list is periodically revised by Ministry of Justice ordinance, and a 2025 reform began requiring registered phonetic readings (フリガナ) of names — verify current character/reading rules with the member's 役場. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Death Notification (死亡届 / shibō-todoke)
recognitions.authority: Municipal office (市区町村役場) 戸籍課 of the place of death, deceased's domicile-of-record, or notifier's residence — Ministry of Justice Civil Affairs Bureau supervising
recognitions.channel: Member's local 市区町村役場 戸籍課 (often handled by the funeral company as agent); overview e.g. https://www.moj.go.jp/MINJI/minji08.html
recognitions.legalBasis: 戸籍法第86条・第87条 (Family Register Act Arts. 86–87 — death must be notified within 7 days, with attached 死亡診断書/死体検案書 medical death certificate; Art. 87 sets the order of obligated notifiers)
recognitions.notes: BOUNDARY: a musubi funeral / memorial covenant ceremony (Reformed 万人祭司, no clergy) has NO civil-law effect and does NOT discharge the legal death-registration duty. The 死亡届 is a separate statutory step the bereaved (or their funeral-company agent) must complete, and it is the precondition for the cremation/burial permit (see jp-cremation-burial-permit-kaso-kyokasho). Drift: notifier-priority list and 7-day deadline are stable; whether the funeral home files as agent and counter procedures vary by municipality. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Cremation / Burial Permit (火葬許可証・埋葬許可証 / kasō-kyoka-shō)
recognitions.authority: Mayor of the municipality (市町村長) — issued by the same 市区町村役場 戸籍課 on acceptance of the death notification; Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (厚生労働省) supervising the statute
recognitions.channel: Member's local 市区町村役場 戸籍課 (issued together with 死亡届 acceptance); statute overview https://www.mhlw.go.jp/bunya/kenkou/seikatsu-eisei15/
recognitions.legalBasis: 墓地、埋葬等に関する法律第5条 (Cemeteries and Burial Act, Act No. 48 of 1948, Art. 5 — cremation, burial, or reinterment requires the mayor's permit) + 戸籍法 death notification as precondition
recognitions.notes: BOUNDARY: a musubi memorial/committal covenant ceremony (Reformed 万人祭司, no clergy) is NOT a legal authorization to cremate, bury, or inter remains. Only the 市町村長 permit issued under 墓埋法第5条 legally authorizes cremation/burial; the cremated permit, once stamped 火葬執行済, becomes the 埋葬許可証 required to inter ashes. This is a step the bereaved/funeral home obtains from the municipality. Drift: 24-hour post-death waiting rule and permit form are stable nationally, but issuance counters and fees vary by municipality. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Common-Law / De-Facto Marriage status (内縁・事実婚 / naien)
recognitions.authority: No registry authority issues it (status arises by fact); recognized partially by courts and social-insurance bodies (年金事務所 / 日本年金機構, health-insurer)
recognitions.channel: Optional partial documentation: 住民票 with 続柄『夫(未届)・妻(未届)』 at the member's 市区町村役場; pension recognition via 日本年金機構 https://www.nenkin.go.jp/
recognitions.legalBasis: No single statute — 内縁 is a case-law doctrine giving certain quasi-marital effects (e.g. 厚生年金保険法第3条第2項 treats a de-facto spouse as a spouse for survivor benefits); notably it does NOT create inheritance or 戸籍 spousal status under 民法
recognitions.notes: BOUNDARY: a musubi covenant marriage that the couple chooses NOT to register as 婚姻届 may form a 内縁/事実婚, but musubi does NOT confer or certify this — it is a factual status courts/insurers assess case-by-case. It grants some protections (e.g. survivor pension) but NOT 民法 inheritance rights or a joint 戸籍. Confidence medium because 内縁 is doctrine-and-fact based, not a single clean statute; survivor-pension article numbers and proof requirements drift — verify with 年金事務所. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Municipal Partnership Oath/Certificate (自治体パートナーシップ宣誓・証明 / jichitai partnership)
recognitions.authority: Individual municipalities/prefectures (e.g. 渋谷区 by 条例, 世田谷区 by 要綱); no national authority — note: 自治体 variation is the whole point of this entry
recognitions.channel: Member's own municipality LGBT/人権 desk, e.g. 渋谷区 https://www.city.shibuya.tokyo.jp/kusei/shisaku/lgbt/partnership.html ; coverage map https://www.marriageforall.jp/database/partnership/
recognitions.legalBasis: Local 条例 or 要綱 only (e.g. 渋谷区男女平等及び多様性を尊重する社会を推進する条例, 2015); these carry NO national civil-law marriage effect under 民法 — they create administrative recognition within that municipality only
recognitions.notes: BOUNDARY + MUNICIPALITY VARIATION: a musubi covenant ceremony does NOT create and is NOT a municipal partnership certificate. These municipal systems have explicitly NO legal marriage effect (no 戸籍 entry, no inheritance, no parental rights) and bind only the issuing 自治体. Coverage and form (渋谷型 条例 vs 世田谷型 要綱, eligibility, mutual-recognition agreements) differ sharply by municipality — members must apply at their own 自治体. Confidence medium: the roster of adopting municipalities (459+ as of mid-2024) and rules change frequently — confirm current local status. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Civil marriage license application (county clerk) — 婚姻許可証申請
recognitions.authority: County Clerk / County Recorder (or equivalent vital-records office) in the county where the marriage occurs; marriage law is set state-by-state
recognitions.channel: Local county clerk's office. Representative portals: CA — Santa Clara County Clerk-Recorder https://clerkrecorder.santaclaracounty.gov/marriage-birth-and-death/apply-marriage-license and LA County https://www.lavote.gov/home/county-clerk/marriage-licenses-ceremonies ; TX — Travis County Clerk https://countyclerk.traviscountytx.gov/departments/recording/marriage-license/ ; NY — NYC City Clerk https://www.cityclerk.nyc.gov/content/marriage-license
recognitions.legalBasis: State marriage statutes; representative: CA Family Code §§350–360 (issuance of license); TX Family Code ch. 2 subch. A (Application for Marriage License); NY Domestic Relations Law §13 (marriage licenses required). A valid license MUST exist before the ceremony for civil recognition.
recognitions.notes: This is the SEPARATE CIVIL STEP the member must do themselves — musubi does NOT do this and cannot register a civil marriage. A musubi covenant ceremony (Reformed 万人祭司, no clergy class) carries NO civil effect by itself; civil recognition requires (1) this license obtained beforehand and (2) a return/filing afterward (see us-marriage-certificate-return-filing). DRIFT WARNING: fees, ID requirements, waiting periods (e.g. TX has a 72-hour wait, CA generally none), validity windows (often 30–90 days), and per-county procedures change frequently; confirm directly with the specific county clerk. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Officiant return / filing of the signed marriage license — 婚姻証明書の提出
recognitions.authority: The authorized officiant returns the completed license; the County Clerk / local registrar records it and the state vital-records office registers the marriage
recognitions.channel: Same county clerk that issued the license. Example deadlines: CA — officiant returns within 10 days (CA Family Code §359); TX — return within 30 days; NY — officiant files certificate, couple obtains record via NYC City Clerk / NY State DOH Vital Records https://www.health.ny.gov/vital_records/
recognitions.legalBasis: CA Family Code §359 (return of license); TX Family Code §2.206 (recording and return of license); NY Domestic Relations Law §14-a / §15 (registration of marriage). Without a properly returned/recorded certificate the marriage may not be provable as a civil record.
recognitions.notes: The step that actually completes civil recognition AFTER a ceremony. CRITICAL BOUNDARY: only a person authorized under state law (see us-ca/ny/tx officiant entries) may sign and return the license — a musubi covenant ceremony does not satisfy this unless the officiant independently holds state authorization. musubi performs the covenant rite (no clergy class) and never claims to register a civil marriage. DRIFT WARNING: return deadlines and which office records the document vary by state/county and change. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: California — who may solemnize a marriage (officiant authorization) — 婚姻挙行権者(加州)
recognitions.authority: California county clerk (commissioner of civil marriages); religious officiants self-authorized by their denomination
recognitions.channel: California Department of Public Health marriage info: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CHSI/ ; county clerk for Deputy Commissioner of Civil Marriages for a Day
recognitions.legalBasis: CA Family Code §400 (priest, minister, rabbi, or authorized person of any religious denomination, 18+); §401 (county clerk = commissioner of civil marriages); §402 (county may license officials of a nonprofit religious institution registered with the Secretary of State)
recognitions.notes: INFORMATIONAL map of who CA recognizes as able to make a ceremony civilly effective. A musubi covenant officiant has civil effect ONLY if independently qualifying under §400 (as an 'authorized person of any religious denomination') AND a valid license is present and returned — musubi makes no representation that any of its officiants so qualify. Reformed 万人祭司 means no clergy class, which may complicate §400/§402 reliance; the member must verify their officiant's standing themselves. DRIFT WARNING: §400 text amended in recent sessions (tenets/refusal language); confirm current version. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: New York — by whom a marriage must be solemnized — 婚姻挙行権者(NY)
recognitions.authority: New York: clergy/ministers (per Religious Corporations Law §2), Ethical Culture leaders, judges, mayors, city/town/village clerks; NYC City Clerk for civil ceremonies
recognitions.channel: NY State DOH Vital Records https://www.health.ny.gov/vital_records/ ; NYC City Clerk https://www.cityclerk.nyc.gov/ ; statute text https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/DOM/11
recognitions.legalBasis: NY Domestic Relations Law §11 (by whom a marriage must be solemnized); cross-references Religious Corporations Law §2 (definition of 'clergyman or minister'). §11 lists clergy/ministers, Ethical Culture leaders, and specified civil officers as the exclusive set of authorized solemnizers.
recognitions.notes: NY is comparatively strict: §11 ties religious solemnizing authority to a 'clergyman or minister' as defined in Religious Corporations Law §2. A musubi covenant rite (no clergy class, 万人祭司) may NOT map cleanly onto this definition, so a member in NY may need a separately-authorized officiant or a civil ceremony for civil recognition. INFORMATIONAL ONLY — musubi does not opine on whether any given officiant satisfies §11. DRIFT WARNING: NY courts have litigated whether online-ordination officiants satisfy §11 (varies by county/borough — historically contested in NYC); confirm locally. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Texas — persons authorized to conduct a marriage ceremony — 婚姻挙行権者(TX)
recognitions.authority: Texas: licensed/ordained Christian minister or priest, Jewish rabbi, an officer of a religious organization authorized by that organization, or a current/former/retired federal or state judge
recognitions.channel: Texas county clerk (issues license, records return); Texas State Law Library guide https://guides.sll.texas.gov/marriage-in-texas/conducting-the-ceremony
recognitions.legalBasis: TX Family Code §2.202 (persons authorized to conduct ceremony). §2.202(c): knowingly conducting a ceremony without authorization is a Class A misdemeanor.
recognitions.notes: TX §2.202(a)(3) explicitly recognizes 'an officer of a religious organization who is authorized by the organization to conduct a marriage ceremony' — comparatively accommodating to a musubi covenant officiant, PROVIDED the organization authorizes them and the license is properly returned. Note §2.202(c) criminal penalty for unauthorized conduct — a member must confirm their officiant's authorization before relying on a musubi rite for civil effect. INFORMATIONAL ONLY; musubi confers no civil status. DRIFT WARNING: TX does NOT separately license/register officiants with the state, so 'authorization' is internal to the religious organization — verify. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Name change after marriage via Social Security (SS-5) — 婚姻後の改名(SSA)
recognitions.authority: U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA); state DMV and U.S. State Department (passport) follow as downstream agencies
recognitions.channel: SSA 'Change name with Social Security' https://www.ssa.gov/number-card/change-name ; Form SS-5 https://www.ssa.gov/forms/ss-5.pdf ; agency-notification overview https://www.usa.gov/name-change
recognitions.legalBasis: Social Security Act §205(c) / 20 C.F.R. §422.107 (evidence to support SSN-record changes); a certified marriage certificate serves as the legal name-change event — no court order is required for a marriage-based name change in the US
recognitions.notes: Relevant to the NAMING dimension of musubi (taking a covenant/married name). A musubi naming ceremony has NO civil effect on legal name; the member must separately update the SSN record (SS-5 + certified marriage certificate) and then DMV/passport. SSA recommends waiting ~30 days post-marriage. A NON-marriage name change (e.g. a chosen covenant name without marriage) generally DOES require a state court order — different process, varies by state. DRIFT WARNING: online-eligible states (~21) and accepted document forms change; SSA does not accept photocopies/notarized copies, only originals or issuer-certified copies. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Death registration + disposition permit (funeral / burial) — 死亡届と埋葬許可
recognitions.authority: Local registrar / state office of vital statistics; a funeral director (or person acting as such) typically files the death certificate and obtains the authorization for final disposition
recognitions.channel: State vital-records office. Representative: CA CDPH Vital Records https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CHSI/Pages/Vital-Records.aspx ; TX DSHS Vital Statistics https://www.dshs.texas.gov/vital-statistics ; NY DOH Vital Records https://www.health.ny.gov/vital_records/ (NYC: separate Bureau of Vital Statistics)
recognitions.legalBasis: State vital-statistics statutes patterned on the CDC/NCHS Model State Vital Statistics Act (death certificate must be filed with the local registrar within a state-set time limit and BEFORE final disposition; a burial-transit / disposition permit authorizes burial, cremation, or transport). E.g. CA Health & Safety Code §§102775 et seq.; TX Health & Safety Code ch. 193 & §711; NY Public Health Law art. 41.
recognitions.notes: Relevant to the FUNERAL/memorial dimension of musubi. A musubi memorial/covenant funeral rite has NO civil effect — death must still be registered and a disposition permit obtained through the civil vital-records system; this is a separate step the family/funeral director performs. musubi does not file death certificates, issue permits, or act as a funeral establishment. INFORMATIONAL ONLY (and note many states regulate who may handle remains / file — often a licensed funeral director). DRIFT WARNING: filing deadlines, whether families may self-file without a funeral director (a few states permit it, most route through a director), and exact statute sections vary widely by state — confirm with the state vital-records office. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. recognitions.title: EU public-documents free movement — apostille exemption for civil-status certificates (Verordnung (EU) 2016/1191 / Règlement (UE) 2016/1191)
recognitions.authority: European Commission, DG Justice and Consumers; implemented by each Member State's civil-registration authorities (e.g. German Standesamt, French mairie / service de l'état civil)
recognitions.channel: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/policies/justice-and-fundamental-rights/civil-justice/family-law/public-documents_en (and e-Justice portal: https://e-justice.europa.eu/topics/your-rights/public-documents_en )
recognitions.legalBasis: Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 July 2016 on promoting the free movement of citizens by simplifying the requirements for presenting certain public documents in the EU (in application since 16 Feb 2019); amends Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012
recognitions.notes: Relevant after a member's CIVIL status is already established: when a member must present a civil birth/name/marriage/death certificate (issued by one Member State, e.g. France or Germany) to authorities in another Member State, this Regulation removes the apostille requirement and offers a multilingual standard form to avoid translation. It covers ONLY public (state-issued civil) documents — it does NOT apply to a musubi covenant-ceremony record, which has no civil-document status. This entry maps a downstream cross-border step the member does themselves. Drift: scope and standard-form list are periodically updated by the Commission; verify current covered-document list before relying. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Germany — compulsory civil marriage at the registry office (Eheschließung beim Standesamt / Zivilehe)
recognitions.authority: Standesamt (local civil registry office) of the place of residence/marriage; supervised under the Personenstandsgesetz (PStG)
recognitions.channel: Local municipal Standesamt (find via the BMI service portal https://www.amtlich-einfach.de or the relevant city's Bürgeramt/Standesamt page, e.g. https://www.berlin.de/standesaemter/ ). Federal overview: https://www.germany.info/us-en/service/04-familymatters/marriage-in-germany-922550
recognitions.legalBasis: Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch (BGB) §§ 1310 ff. (marriage concluded before the registrar); Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) § 11 (Eheschließung). Since 1876 only a civil marriage before the Standesbeamter has legal effect; a religious ceremony has no civil effect (the former prohibition on religious ceremony before civil marriage was lifted in 2009)
recognitions.notes: In Germany a musubi covenant ceremony has NO civil-marriage effect; the member must separately conclude a civil marriage before the Standesamt for legal recognition. Since 2009 the religious/covenant ceremony may take place before, after, or independently of the civil step — no legal ordering requirement (unlike France). This maps where the separate civil step lives. Drift: exact documents required and appointment process vary by Land and municipality; verify with the specific Standesamt. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: France — civil marriage at the town hall, mandatory before any religious ceremony (Mariage civil à la mairie ; antériorité obligatoire)
recognitions.authority: Officier de l'état civil at the mairie (town hall) of the commune of one spouse's domicile/residence
recognitions.channel: Local mairie / service de l'état civil. Official procedure overview: https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F930
recognitions.legalBasis: Code civil art. 165 (marriage celebrated publicly in a republican ceremony before the officier de l'état civil) and arts. 63 ff. (banns / dossier); Code pénal art. 433-21 (a minister of any religion who habitually performs a religious marriage ceremony without proof of the prior civil marriage act is liable to 1 year imprisonment and a €7,500 fine — penalty strengthened by Loi n° 2021-1109 du 24 août 2021 confortant le respect des principes de la République)
recognitions.notes: CRITICAL France-specific boundary: only the civil marriage at the mairie carries legal effect, and a religious/covenant ceremony must NOT habitually precede the civil marriage (Code pénal art. 433-21 penalises the officiant on the second occurrence — 'délit d'habitude'). A musubi covenant ceremony confers NO civil status and, in France, should follow the civil marriage. This entry flags a real legal-ordering constraint the member must observe. Drift: penalty amounts/wording amended by the 2021 law — verify current Code pénal text. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.

recognitions.title: Germany — death registration and death certificate at the registry office (Sterbefall-Anzeige / Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt)
recognitions.authority: Standesamt of the place where the death occurred
recognitions.channel: Standesamt of the place of death (city Standesamt page, e.g. https://www.schwerin.de or https://www.berlin.de/standesaemter/ ). In practice the funeral director (Bestatter) often files on the family's behalf.
recognitions.legalBasis: Personenstandsgesetz (PStG) § 28 — every death must be reported to the Standesamt of the place of death no later than the third working day after the death; the registrar enters it in the death register and issues the Sterbeurkunde (§§ 28–33 PStG)
recognitions.notes: A musubi memorial/funeral covenant ceremony carries NO civil effect; the legally required step is the civil death registration at the Standesamt (PStG § 28), which produces the Sterbeurkunde needed for burial/cremation, inheritance, and deregistration. This maps the separate civil step. Drift: the reporting deadline and who is obligated to report are set in PStG and may be supplemented by Land burial laws (Bestattungsgesetze) — verify locally. musubi performs covenant ceremonies (Reformed 万人祭司, NO clergy class), it does NOT confer civil status. This registry is INFORMATIONAL only — it maps where a civil step is separately required; it gives no legal advice and never claims to register a civil marriage.
